text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shoot(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
Unblockable(x, y) ::: x cannot block y's shooting.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Michael(T) ∧ ∀x (Man(x) → Taller(x, T)) ::: Michael is a man taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Peter(P) ∧ Taller(P, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
Michael can block any shooter who does not jump when shooting ::: (∀x (Shoot(x, y) → (CanBlock(Michael, y) ∧ ¬Jump(x)))).
Michael cannot block Windy's shooting ::: ¬CanBlock(Michael, Windy).
Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter ::: ∀x (Shoot(x, y) ∧ Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)).
Conclusion:
Peter is shorter than a man in Michael's class ::: ∃x (Man(x) ∧ Taller(x, Peter))
